# Figures {#sec-g-figures}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("../_setup.R")
sc <- synth_counts(n_per_group = 4)
fdr <- report_param("fdr")
lfc <- report_param("lfc_threshold")
kept <- rowMeans(sc$counts) >= report_param("min_count")
de <- synth_de(n_per_group = 4)[kept, ]
de$FDR <- p.adjust(de$p, method = "BH")
de$call <- factor(ifelse(de$FDR < fdr & de$log2FC >= lfc, "up",
                  ifelse(de$FDR < fdr & de$log2FC <= -lfc, "down", "ns")),
                  levels = c("up", "down", "ns"))
lib <- colSums(sc$counts)
logcpm <- log2(t(t(sc$counts + 1) / (lib + 1) * 1e6))[kept, ]
```

Every figure has a label, a caption, and alt text. The caption says what is plotted, n, the encoding, any threshold lines, and whether scales are shared. The alt text says what a sighted reader would see.

## A single figure {#sec-g-figures-basic}

```{r}
#| label: fig-g-figures-basic
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of log2 fold change for all tested synthetic features, in bins of 0.25 log2 units. Dashed lines mark the fold-change thresholds."
#| fig-alt: "A histogram centred on zero with long, thin tails on both sides beyond the dashed threshold lines."
ggplot(de, aes(log2FC)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, fill = HOUSE_PAL[["down"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-lfc, lfc), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (treated / control)", y = "Features")
```

````markdown
```{{r}}
#| label: fig-g-figures-basic
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of log2 fold change for all tested synthetic features, in bins of 0.25 log2 units. Dashed lines mark the fold-change thresholds."
#| fig-alt: "A histogram centred on zero with long, thin tails on both sides beyond the dashed threshold lines."
ggplot(de, aes(log2FC)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25)
```
````

## Significance by shape and colour {#sec-g-figures-volcano}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## How to read this
Each point is one feature. Triangles pointing up rose, and triangles pointing down fell. Grey circles did not pass both thresholds. Shape carries the call on its own, so the figure reads in greyscale.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-g-figures-volcano
#| fig-cap: "Log2 fold change against minus log10 p-value for each tested synthetic feature. Shape and colour both show the call. Dashed lines mark the fold-change thresholds."
#| fig-alt: "A volcano plot. Most points are grey circles near the bottom centre. A few triangles sit higher up, beyond the dashed lines on each side."
p_volcano <- ggplot(de, aes(log2FC, -log10(p), colour = call, shape = call)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-lfc, lfc), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = HOUSE_PAL[c("up", "down", "ns")], drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(up = 17, down = 25, ns = 16), drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (treated / control)", y = "-log10 p", colour = "Call", shape = "Call")
p_volcano
```

### What this figure cannot be used as evidence for {#sec-g-figures-evidence}

This figure cannot be used as evidence that the grey features are unaffected. Their changes may sit below the detection floor of a four-sample design. It also says nothing about why any feature moved.

## Multi-panel figures {#sec-g-figures-panels}

```{r}
#| label: fig-g-figures-panels
#| fig-cap: "Mean log CPM per feature in each group, for all tested synthetic features. Both panels share the same axes."
#| fig-subcap:
#|   - "Control group."
#|   - "Treated group."
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "A histogram of mean log CPM for the control group, with one broad peak."
#|   - "A histogram of mean log CPM for the treated group, with one broad peak of the same shape."
#| layout-ncol: 2
treated <- sc$samples$group == "treated"
for (g in c("control", "treated")) {
  cols <- if (g == "treated") treated else !treated
  print(ggplot(data.frame(m = rowMeans(logcpm[, cols])), aes(m)) +
          geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, fill = HOUSE_PAL[["down"]]) +
          coord_cartesian(xlim = range(logcpm), ylim = c(0, 80)) +
          labs(x = "Mean log CPM", y = "Features"))
}
```

Use `layout-ncol` with `fig-subcap` when the reader must compare panels side by side. State in the caption whether the axes are shared.

## One figure per group in tabs {#sec-g-figures-tabset}

::: {.panel-tabset}
```{r}
#| results: asis
#| fig-alt: "A histogram of log CPM for every feature in one sample, with one broad peak."
for (s in colnames(logcpm)[c(1, 5)]) {
  cat("\n\n### Sample ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(ggplot(data.frame(v = logcpm[, s]), aes(v)) +
          geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, fill = HOUSE_PAL[["down"]]) +
          labs(x = "log CPM", y = "Features", title = paste("Sample", s)))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```
:::

The loop writes one tab heading and one figure per item, with `results: asis`. Use it for the same figure repeated for each group, sample, or contrast.

## Heatmaps of row z-scores {#sec-g-figures-heatmap}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## How to read this
Each row is one feature, scaled to its own mean and standard deviation. A dark cell is far from that feature's own mean. A pale cell is a small difference from that mean, not low expression. A z-score is not absolute expression.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-g-figures-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Row z-scores of log CPM for the 20 synthetic features with the smallest p-values, across all eight samples. Colour runs from below to above each feature's own mean."
#| fig-alt: "A grid of 20 rows and 8 columns. For most rows, the four control columns share one colour and the four treated columns share the other."
top <- head(de[order(de$p), "gene"], 20)
z <- t(scale(t(logcpm[top, ])))
hm <- data.frame(gene = rep(rownames(z), ncol(z)), sample = rep(colnames(z), each = nrow(z)),
                 z = as.vector(z))
hm$gene <- factor(hm$gene, levels = rev(top))
ggplot(hm, aes(sample, gene, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = HOUSE_PAL[["down"]], mid = "#f7f7f7", high = HOUSE_PAL[["up"]]) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Row z-score")
```

## Categories with Okabe-Ito colours {#sec-g-figures-scatter}

```{r}
#| label: fig-g-figures-scatter
#| fig-cap: "A synthetic two-dimensional embedding of 900 points in three clusters, coloured with the Okabe-Ito palette."
#| fig-alt: "A scatter plot of three separate clouds of points, each in its own colour."
emb <- synth_embedding()
ggplot(emb, aes(dim1, dim2, colour = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = OKABE_ITO) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Dimension 1", y = "Dimension 2", colour = NULL)
```

## Saving figures for papers {#sec-g-figures-save}

```{r}
paths <- save_figure(p_volcano, "g02-volcano", width = 6, height = 4)
basename(paths)
```

`save_figure()` writes the same plot as PDF and PNG into `figures/`. That folder is in `.gitignore`, so rendered figures never enter history.
